title: Paint or Flooring First? The Right Order for a Renovation
description: In most renovations, paint walls and ceilings after demolition and drywall work but before new flooring goes in. Then touch up baseboards after the floors are installed. Here's why, and the exceptions.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: in most renovations, paint after demolition and drywall work but before new flooring goes in. Then do a final baseboard and touch-up pass after the floors are installed. That order keeps paint off your new floors and keeps flooring dust off your fresh walls.

The Usual Renovation Order

  1. Demolition and removal of old flooring, cabinets or fixtures

  2. Rough work: electrical, plumbing and any framing

  3. Drywall repair, texture and sanding, the dustiest stage

  4. Prime and paint ceilings and walls

  5. Install flooring

  6. Install or reinstall baseboards, then caulk, fill and paint them

  7. Final touch-ups for any scuffs from the flooring crew

Why Painting Before Flooring Usually Wins

  • No risk to new floors. Drips, ladder feet and dragged equipment can't damage floors that aren't there yet.

  • Faster, cheaper painting. Bare subfloor needs less protection, so the crew spends more time painting and less time masking.

  • Cleaner cut lines. Walls can be painted all the way down, and the baseboards cover the bottom edge.

When Flooring Should Go First

  • Hardwood that needs sanding and refinishing on site. Sanding creates a lot of fine dust. Many people refinish the floors first and then paint, or at least do the final coat of finish last. Coordinate the order with your flooring contractor.

  • Only the floors are changing. If the walls aren't being painted, skip ahead and protect the walls during installation.

  • Tight timelines. Sometimes the flooring crew's schedule decides the order. Then plan for extra floor protection and a touch-up pass.

Tips to Keep the Two Trades From Undoing Each Other

  • Save a labeled can of each wall and trim color for touch-ups after flooring

  • Ask flooring installers to protect painted walls when they carry in materials

  • Hold off on final baseboard paint until after the floors are in

  • Build a day for touch-ups into the end of the schedule

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I paint before or after installing new baseboards?

Paint the walls first. Install the baseboards after the floors, then caulk, fill nail holes and paint them in place for the cleanest result.

Should I paint before or after new carpet?

Before, ideally. Carpet is the hardest flooring to clean paint off of.

Do painters work around new floors?

Yes. Professional painters protect finished floors with drop cloths, rosin paper or floor protection film. It just takes more setup time.
